nodes.summary: The column-centered data matrix `X i j - x̄ⱼ`.
nodes.title: Column-centered data matrix

nodes.summary: The sample mean of column `j` of an `n × p` data matrix (rows are observations). For `n = 0` it is the junk value `0`.
nodes.title: Sample mean of a data matrix column

nodes.summary: The quadratic form expanded in the ordered eigenbasis: `xᵀ S x = ∑ λᵢ ⟪vᵢ, x⟫²`.
nodes.title: Quadratic form expanded in the ordered eigenbasis

nodes.summary: Every subspace of dimension `p - k` contains a nonzero vector whose Rayleigh quotient is at least `λₖ`.
nodes.title: Courant–Fischer min–max, matrix form

nodes.summary: Every subspace of dimension `k + 1` contains a nonzero vector whose Rayleigh quotient is at most `λₖ`.
nodes.title: Courant–Fischer max–min, matrix form

nodes.summary: The squared Frobenius error of the truncated SVD is the sum of the discarded squared singular values.
nodes.title: Frobenius error of the truncated SVD

nodes.summary: The truncated SVD is a best rank-`k` approximation of `A` in the Frobenius norm: the least squared distance from `A` to a matrix of rank at most `k` is `∑_{k ≤ i < n} σᵢ²`, attained by `truncSVD A k`.
nodes.title: Eckart–Young, best-approximation form

nodes.summary: Dual of `rayleigh_le_of_orthogonal`: on nonzero directions orthogonal to the eigenvectors after index `k`, the Rayleigh quotient is at least the `k`-th eigenvalue.
nodes.title: Lower bound on the Rayleigh quotient for orthogonal directions

nodes.summary: The `k`-th basis vector is an eigenvector for the `k`-th eigenvalue.
nodes.title: Ordered eigenbasis vectors are eigenvectors

nodes.summary: An orthonormal eigenbasis of a real symmetric matrix, ordered to match `orderedEigenvalues`; for a covariance matrix these are the principal axes.
nodes.title: Ordered orthonormal eigenbasis of a symmetric matrix

nodes.summary: The ordered eigenvalues are decreasing.
nodes.title: Ordered eigenvalues are decreasing

nodes.summary: The eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite matrix are nonnegative.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite matrix are nonnegative

nodes.summary: The eigenvalues `λ₀ ≥ λ₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_{p-1}` of a real symmetric `p × p` matrix, in decreasing order (Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.eigenvalues` of `Matrix.toEuclideanLin S`).
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix in decreasing order

nodes.summary: The truncated SVD has rank at most `k`.
nodes.title: Rank of the truncated SVD is at most k

nodes.summary: On nonzero directions orthogonal to the first `k` eigenvectors, the Rayleigh quotient is at most the `k`-th eigenvalue; the bound is attained at the `k`-th eigenvector (`rayleigh_orderedEigenbasis`).
nodes.title: Hotelling's characterization of the principal axes

nodes.summary: The Rayleigh quotient of the `k`-th eigenvector is the `k`-th eigenvalue.
nodes.title: Rayleigh quotient of an eigenvector is its eigenvalue

nodes.summary: The Rayleigh quotient `wᵀ S w / wᵀ w` of a real matrix (junk value `0` at `w = 0`).
nodes.title: Rayleigh quotient of a matrix

nodes.summary: Right singular vectors of `A`: an orthonormal eigenbasis of `Aᵀ A`, ordered so that the `i`-th vector has eigenvalue `σᵢ²` with `σ₀ ≥ σ₁ ≥ ⋯` the singular values.
nodes.title: Right singular vectors of a matrix

nodes.summary: Entries of the sample covariance matrix: `Sⱼₖ = (n - 1)⁻¹ ∑ᵢ (Xᵢⱼ - x̄ⱼ)(Xᵢₖ - x̄ₖ)`.
nodes.title: Entries of the sample covariance matrix

nodes.summary: The sample covariance matrix is symmetric.
nodes.title: Sample covariance matrix is symmetric

nodes.summary: The sample covariance matrix is positive semidefinite (for every `n`).
nodes.title: Sample covariance matrix is positive semidefinite

nodes.summary: The unbiased sample covariance matrix `(n - 1)⁻¹ (X - x̄)ᵀ (X - x̄)` of an `n × p` data matrix. The divisor needs `2 ≤ n`; for `n = 1` the factor is the junk value `(0 : ℝ)⁻¹ = 0` (and for `n = 0` the product is the zero matrix).
nodes.title: Unbiased sample covariance matrix

nodes.summary: The sample variance of the scores along `w` is the quadratic form `wᵀ S w`.
nodes.title: Sample variance of scores is a quadratic form

nodes.summary: The principal-component scores `(X - x̄) w` of the observations along a direction `w`.
nodes.title: Principal component scores

nodes.summary: The centered columns sum to zero (for at least one observation).
nodes.title: Centered columns sum to zero

nodes.summary: The ordered eigenvalues sum to the trace.
nodes.title: Ordered eigenvalues sum to the trace

nodes.summary: The scores along any direction have sample mean zero.
nodes.title: Principal component scores have sample mean zero

nodes.summary: Every matrix of rank at most `k` has squared Frobenius distance from `A` at least the sum of the discarded squared singular values.
nodes.title: Eckart–Young (Frobenius norm)

nodes.summary: The trace of the sample covariance matrix is the total sample variance, the sum of the column sample variances.
nodes.title: Trace of the sample covariance is the total sample variance

nodes.summary: The rank-`k` truncated singular value decomposition `A Vₖ Vₖᵀ = ∑_{i<k} σᵢ uᵢ vᵢᵀ`, where `Vₖ` collects the first `k` right singular vectors.
nodes.title: Truncated singular value decomposition

nodes.summary: The proportion of variance explained is at most one.
nodes.title: Proportion of variance explained is at most one

nodes.summary: Keeping more components explains more variance.
nodes.title: More components explain more variance

nodes.summary: The proportion of variance explained is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Proportion of variance explained is nonnegative

nodes.summary: All `p` components explain all of the variance, when the total variance is positive.
nodes.title: All components explain all of the variance

nodes.summary: The proportion of total sample variance explained by the first `k` principal components: `(λ₀ + ⋯ + λ_{k-1}) / tr S` for the sample covariance matrix `S`. The junk value `0` is returned when the total variance `tr S` is `0` (constant data).
nodes.title: Proportion of variance explained by principal components

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
